assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the gut hormone's insulinotropic action to stable long-acting agonists, produced transformative therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity with large, durable clinical and societal impact. Original physiological discovery and translation form one coherent arc.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 biology and its therapeutic rationale; Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is a decisive contribution. Habener-type contributions and industrial development (Knudsen) are not in the supplied credit, so a three-person split leaves some contested allocation.
assessment.maturity: Extensive independent confirmation across many large outcome trials; the therapeutic effect is firmly established and the timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over the identification of the active peptide and who was first
Whether industrial peptide-engineering credit (Knudsen) should displace a physiological discoverer
My recollection of the discovery chronology is not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality; the concept, design of costimulation and clinical proof are all significant.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain made the central CAR design and clinical translation contributions; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early clinical CAR work. Other contributors (e.g., Eshhar, Kuwana, Brenner) lie outside the supplied credit, so the trio is defensible but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of clinical follow-up; remaining questions concern solid tumours and toxicity, not the core discovery.
uncertainties: Early conceptual credit (first-generation CAR concepts) is outside the supplied names
Compound discovery of concept, costimulation and clinical proof may need different recognition

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new principle of intracellular signaling from the ER to the nucleus, with consequences for secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. A clean, original and deeply influential cell-biological discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the pathway (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing) and are the natural core; the supplied credit is compact and plausible for a prize.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed across yeast and mammals for 25 years; therapeutic modulation is still developing, but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Medical impact is more indirect than for therapeutic candidates
Roles of other contributors such as Shamu or Ron are not in the credited names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity and transformed experimental physiology; microbial opsins as tools are an invention of broad and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed among channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier concepts (Miesenböck); six names exceed the three-laureate limit, so any selection is a contested judgement.
assessment.maturity: Methodologically mature and widely used; clinical translation (vision restoration) is early but not needed for the basic claim.
uncertainties: Attribution among six credited people is genuinely unresolved
Tool-based impact versus disease relevance may weigh differently with the full committee

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established molecularly targeted therapy, converting CML from a fatal disease into a chronic condition, and the resistance work of Sawyers shaped the field's second-generation agents.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical translation), Lydon (compound development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms) form a reasonable trio; Rowley, Nowell and Witte's earlier discoveries are not in the credited set, so earlier foundational credit is partly missing.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of follow-up and a paradigm well confirmed; recognition is arguably overdue and Lasker-recognised.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as clinical translation overlapping earlier recognised chromosome work

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing has rewritten genomics, diagnostics and cancer medicine, and is a technology of extraordinary scale and lasting impact. The sequencing-by-synthesis concept and its implementation are clear, original inventions.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the Solexa chemistry and Mayer the parallel clonal-cluster concept; other technology inventors (e.g., Church, Rothberg, Shendure) and the contested corporate lineage complicate allocation. I work in related genomic methods but have no documented involvement here.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with universal adoption; the main question is credit rather than timing.
uncertainties: Substantial dispute over which sequencing inventions merit recognition and how to apportion them
Prize fit as technology rather than a physiological or medical discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR signaling uncovered a central nutrient-sensing growth regulator, with consequences for metabolism, ageing, immunosuppression and cancer; the discovery is fundamental and has proven therapeutic offshoots.
assessment.attribution: Hall's discovery of TOR and Schreiber's rapamycin-target chemical biology are foundational; Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work is important but his inclusion may be contentious, so I would avoid relying on him. Other early contributors (Heitman, Movva, Hall's colleagues) are outside the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed and extensively replicated; clinical use of rapalogs is established, broader therapeutic payoff is still emerging.
uncertainties: Sabatini's standing and the fairness of three-person allocation
Whether clinical impact outside transplantation and oncology is sufficient

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, with measured population-level reductions in disease; a clear, high-impact translational achievement with direct public-health benefit.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (VLP assembly) and Frazer (VLP vaccine development) are central; Zhou, Kirnbauer and Cervical Cancer vaccine-industry teams are not in the supplied credit. Allocation among near-simultaneous groups is partly unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness now documented over more than a decade; recognition is timely, with zur Hausen's earlier prize covering the virus-cancer link.
uncertainties: Priority among parallel VLP groups remains contested
Relationship to the existing HPV-cancer prize may reduce novelty in the committee's view
